response.text:
Accrual and cash-basis accounting are two ways to track your business money. With cash-basis, you record income only when you actually receive payment and record expenses only when you pay them. It’s simple and shows how much cash you have on hand.

Accrual accounting records income when you earn it (even if the customer hasn’t paid yet) and records expenses when they happen (even if you haven’t paid them yet). That means you include money customers owe you and bills you haven’t paid yet. Accrual gives a more complete picture of your business activity over time, because it matches sales and the costs tied to them, not just when cash moves.

For day-to-day cash decisions, cash-basis can be easier. For understanding overall performance, planning, or if you have customers who pay later, accrual is usually more informative. Choose the method that fits your business size and needs.
